messages:
Mike R.: Heads up — after the canary of fast-kernel-2 we see steady mem climb on long streaming-toolloop runs. starts ~8–12m in, ~200MB/min growth.
Anya S.: Confirmed on my dedicated sim. Not a leak in the python harness (same repro in C++) — profile points at kv_page + refcounting hotspots.
Liam K.: Do we have jemalloc stats and pmap from the instance? also kernel choice bump changed vectorized attention path, could affect KV cache layout.
Mike R.: Paste of quick dumps:
```
$ pmap -x 12345 | tail -n1
12345:  6.3G total  5.4G resident  0K shared  0K text  4.9G data
$ jemalloc stats
allocated: 4.9G
active: 5.2G
metadata: 120M
arena.0.cached: 30M
$ /app/bin/kv-metrics dump | head -n20
kv_pages_total: 1_234_567
kv_pages_in_use: 870_112
kv_page_refs_live: 870_080
kv_page_refs_stale: 32
evict_policy: adaptive_age
```
Looks like pages_in_use keeps climbing while total refs roughly equal — small delta of stale refs grows.
Sofia P.: I also grabbed vmstat during the run: high majflt/sec spike as growth accelerates. That suggests paging rather than pure allocator leak.
Anya S.: Hypothesis: new kernel path changed prefetch timing -> more pages pinned longer in KV cache due to async prefetch + delayed ref release on the toolloop path. We saw similar with batcher prefetch before.
Liam K.: Could be batching heuristics interacting: fast-kernel-2 reduces per-token latency so batch windows shorter -> more small batches -> cache churn increases, more temporary page allocations and delayed eviction.
Mike R.: Repro steps I used: stress-toolloop --model=redwood/llama-8k --stream --tools=10 --session-length=30k --prefetch=on --batching.max_wait_ms=2. Repro consistent in ~10m.
Anya S.: I ran with prefetch=off and growth stops — interesting. Means prefetch path likely leaking refs or holding onto slices.
Liam K.: Can we get a sampling heap with symbols? run:
```
$ perf record -F 99 -g -p 12345 -- sleep 60
$ perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > perf.folded
$ flamegraph.pl perf.folded > perf.svg
```
Would like to see allocations attributed to kv_ref_hold or prefetch callbacks.
Mike R.: Attached perf snippet (excerpt):
```
# top stacks
kv_prefetch_cb
kv_page_pin
tensor_chunk_alloc
refcount_incr
```
Suggests prefetch callback does refcount incr without matching release under async cancel.
Sofia P.: Also, reviewing kernel diff, fast-kernel-2 added early-kv-cache-touch to warm KV pages before attention kernel runs. probably racing with eviction when long contexts extend lifespan.
deploy-bot: deploy canary fast-kernel-2 to prod-canaries at 2026-03-15T21:12:03Z :rocket:
Liam K.: Action items: 1) Anya to run ASAN build of runtime with prefetch instrumentation and toggles (prefetch off/on, early-touch off). 2) Mike to capture jemalloc epoch dumps over time and pmap snapshots every 2m. 3) I'll add a debug metric: kv_prefetch_inflight_count + kv_prefetch_cancel_count.
Anya S.: Started ASAN run now, will flip prefetch hooks and post heapdiffs.
Mike R.: I'll add a short reproducer job in perf infra with both kernels to compare; tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform.
Liam K.: If ASAN repros, we should be able to pinpoint missing ref release in prefetch cancel path. If not, next suspect: batching window change -> allocator fragmentation.
Sofia P.: For the fragmentation angle, please also collect mallctl stats: extent fragmentation, retained vs active.
Mike R.: Noted. Will upload all artifacts to the thread. Thanks — making this a blocker for next patch release until we root cause. :eyes:
